game.name: pudge-wars-basic
game.description: BASIC and neural file policies in a deterministic river arena, with optional Jev judgments. Two teams of butchers hook, blink and fight to the kill goal.

wait_for_llm.description: Wait for all seats’ concurrent LLM/Jev requests between simulation ticks.

player.value: Upload raw UTF-8 BASIC source (up to 64 KiB) or a ZIP package (up to 16 MiB, 256 files) containing exactly one .bas entry and read-only model resources. Files are detected by content, including extensionless staged uploads. One isolated Bassy VM per seat: persistent variables and tensors, 100,000 instructions and 250,000 work units per decision, 2 MiB BASIC memory and 32 MiB native tensor memory. Use GotA-compatible tensor operations and tensors.json to implement feed-forward or recurrent neural networks in BASIC. The policy constructs fog-clipped observations and issues ordinary game actions; model outputs never bypass game rules. Host action arguments require exact integers; / is Q16.16 division and \ is integer division. Optional LLM and Jev oracle functions use the host-configured sidecar, with X-Coworld-Player-Slot attribution. No credentials or arbitrary filesystem/network access are exposed to BASIC. wait_for_llm defaults to true: all seats submit concurrently, then the host waits between ticks for replies or timeouts. With async requests or external inference, live runs need not reproduce identical actions; action replays remain verifiable. PRINT, diagnostics and annotations are private to the seat. Compilation/package errors fail the attributed seat; runtime errors disable only that VM. See the bundled BASIC, neural ZIP and Jev examples and coworld/INFERENCE.md.

global.value: GET /healthz reports readiness. /global is the global spectator WebSocket with Ping/Pong. /client/global serves the global snapshot viewer. Completed episodes use the bundled WASM replay viewer. League episodes do not accept human or JSON policy actions.

readme.value:
# Pudge Wars BASIC and neural policies

Upload raw UTF-8 BASIC source (up to 64 KiB) or a ZIP package (up to 16 MiB, 256 files) containing exactly one .bas entry and read-only model resources. Files are detected by content, including extensionless staged uploads. One isolated Bassy VM per seat: persistent variables and tensors, 100,000 instructions and 250,000 work units per decision, 2 MiB BASIC memory and 32 MiB native tensor memory. Use GotA-compatible tensor operations and tensors.json to implement feed-forward or recurrent neural networks in BASIC. The policy constructs fog-clipped observations and issues ordinary game actions; model outputs never bypass game rules. Host action arguments require exact integers; / is Q16.16 division and \ is integer division. Optional LLM and Jev oracle functions use the host-configured sidecar, with X-Coworld-Player-Slot attribution. No credentials or arbitrary filesystem/network access are exposed to BASIC. wait_for_llm defaults to true: all seats submit concurrently, then the host waits between ticks for replies or timeouts. With async requests or external inference, live runs need not reproduce identical actions; action replays remain verifiable. PRINT, diagnostics and annotations are private to the seat. Compilation/package errors fail the attributed seat; runtime errors disable only that VM. See the bundled BASIC, neural ZIP and Jev examples and coworld/INFERENCE.md.

Slots are contiguous banks: first half West, second half East. league-3v3 uses six seats, first to 30 within 38,400 ticks; duel-1v1 uses two seats, first to 10 within 15,360 ticks. Each winning seat scores 1; losses and draws score 0. At the time limit the bank ahead wins. BASIC can use integer, fixed-point or float32 tensors; float32 is confined to tensor operations. Uploaded native or Python code is never executed. Existing container policies must be rewritten as BASIC or a BASIC-plus-weights package. Game authors can read uploaded policy files.
